title: Winstead's orchestra, the brass band and learning to read
summary: Wilbur Winstead took him into his orchestra and then the brass band; he learned from orchestrations and sheet music and says he had no trumpet-playing brother.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: Did you get into that band then soon?

Well, and, uh, no, I didn't get into the brass band because they had an orchestra there then, was a fellow named Wilbur Winstead, Wilbur Winstead had an orchestra. While then he, uh, he'd taken an interest in me and he put me in his orchestra there, and that way I began to, those different fellas helped me along that way, this is the way I began to learn how to play the trumpet. And then I, uh, he carried me from there, I used to work and reference with him, in his band, and he played in the brass band over in another part of town. Oh, yeah. This band where I was just telling him I used to play the fairs and so on. Oh, yeah. And so he carried me over there to one Sunday, and so they had him bring me back over there, and then I got to play the band, and then all those fellas that just helped me and showed me, you know, helping along. And so that's the way I got started. And there was another fella in there, a very good trumpet player, Robert Williams. He was very good.
Did these boys and fellas all help you to learn music, to read music right away, or did you play by ear at first?
Oh, I started out reading music.
They showed you the scale right away over there. Yes, I started out reading music.

And so that's because I'd go in those bands and I'd play those, they had those orchestrations. Yes. And then afterwards I had playing with piano, just three pieces, piano, trumpet, and drum. Oh, yeah. And we still used the music. We used to get those song sheets in there. Oh, yeah. There was a lot of that sheet music. And we'd play from that and they'd learn how to... You'd transpose. Transpose. And we used to play right off of the... Right off of the... Well, while I think of it, sort of an interruption, one time, a long time ago, somebody told me

you'd been in Louisville and heard some trumpet player by the name of Mitchell and they thought maybe it was your brother. Did you ever have any brothers that played? No. No, no. No, I never had any brothers. So that was a false story then. No, I never had any brothers.
I wondered if it was true. I never had any brothers to play.
